incident.relatedNote: Same login pattern at Sabine Pass LNG
incident.summary: A stolen port authority sign-in was used to reach the Barbours Cut terminal operating system and stop cargo movement in the Houston Ship Channel: berth scheduling is offline, gantry cranes are down and vessel tracking is degraded. Sabine Pass LNG shows the same login pattern; Texas City and Beaumont are on watch.

entities.whyItMatters: Terminal operating system encrypted; berth scheduling offline; vessel tracking degraded.

entities.label: Electricity (grid supply)
entities.whyItMatters: The grid itself is normal. The port's shore power controller (POH-SCADA-01) is at risk because it sits on the same terminal network.

entities.label: Sabine Pass LNG
entities.whyItMatters: Ships load LNG through the port's scheduling. It also shows the same login pattern as the port, so the same access may be used here. Not a confirmed compromise.

entities.label: Colonial Pipeline (refined products)
entities.whyItMatters: Refined products move from Ship Channel terminals into the pipeline. Deliveries slip once tankers can't berth.

entities.label: Product tankers ×47
entities.whyItMatters: Tankers can't be given berths while berth scheduling is offline. They go to anchor, and vessel operations degrade port-wide by 12 h.

entities.label: Beaumont / Port Arthur
entities.whyItMatters: Secondary petroleum port and the Motiva refinery (600,000 barrels a day). Also the first alternative for product tankers, so check it before relying on it.

entities.label: Texas City terminal
entities.whyItMatters: Correlated indicators: same vessel traffic and an operator report of the same sign-in vector. Watch posture.

entities.label: Ship Channel plants
entities.whyItMatters: Plants run on feedstock that arrives through the port. They cut rates by 18 h, and chemical barge loadings stop, including chlorine.

entities.label: Freeport complex
entities.whyItMatters: Same feedstock dependence as the Ship Channel plants.

entities.label: SCP-CL2 chlorine barge loadout
entities.whyItMatters: Chlorine for water plants ships from here. Shipments stop when the Ship Channel plants cut rates.

entities.label: Houston water plants
entities.whyItMatters: Water plants disinfect with chlorine shipped from the Ship Channel. About a day of chlorine is on hand. Chlorine by truck is the backup route, not yet requested.

entities.label: Watershed 250 utilities (first cohort)
entities.whyItMatters: Same chlorine supply as the Houston water plants. This is where the port incident reaches the water sector.

entities.label: Crude tankers
entities.whyItMatters: Crude tankers in the Ship Channel are delayed while berth scheduling is offline.

entities.label: Chemical barges
entities.whyItMatters: Barge loadings at the Ship Channel stop once the plants cut rates.

entities.label: Feedstock pipelines
entities.whyItMatters: Energy-linked feedstock lines into the chemical plants lose supply that arrives through the port.

entities.label: Motiva refinery (Port Arthur)
entities.whyItMatters: 600,000 barrels a day. Monitoring with the Beaumont port.

entities.label: Galveston refinery
entities.whyItMatters: Connected to petroleum flows, but normal in this scenario.
